ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure is a titration curve of pH changing with the volume of NaOH added, with the horizontal axis labeled Volume NaOH (mL), and the vertical axis as pH. The curve starts at low pH, the first neutralization jump appears near about 10 mL, and the second more obvious neutralization jump appears near about 20 mL; 20 mL is near the second equivalence point. Reasoning: The prompt gives that the analyte is the diprotic acid H2C2O4, and the titrant is the strong base NaOH. At the first equivalence point, a diprotic acid has mainly lost one proton to form HC2O4^-; at the second equivalence point, both acidic protons have been neutralized by NaOH. Therefore, when 20 mL NaOH is added, the species from the acid source with the greatest concentration is the fully deprotonated oxalate ion C2O4^2-.

raw_record.question_text: Based on the titration graph, when 20 mL of 0.10 M NaOH has been added to 20 mL of $H_2C_2O_4$, which species is present in the greatest concentration in solution?

method.method_draft: First describe the graph: identify the two neutralization jumps and note that 20 mL lies at the second equivalence point. From the text, the acid is H2C2O4 and the titrant is strong base NaOH. Apply the diprotic-acid titration rule: at the second equivalence point both acidic protons have been neutralized, so the dominant oxalate-containing species is the fully deprotonated conjugate base. Conclude that the greatest concentration species among the acid-derived species is C2O4^2−.
method.CoT_raw: 图像描述：图中是 pH 随加入 NaOH 体积变化的滴定曲线，横轴标为 Volume NaOH (mL)，纵轴为 pH。曲线从低 pH 开始，约在 10 mL 附近出现第一个中和跃变，约在 20 mL 附近出现第二个更明显的中和跃变；20 mL 位于第二个等当点附近。推理：题干给出被滴定物是二元酸 H2C2O4，滴定剂是强碱 NaOH。二元酸在第一个等当点时主要失去一个质子形成 HC2O4^-，在第二个等当点时两个酸性质子都被 NaOH 中和。因此，在 20 mL NaOH 加入时，酸来源物种中占最大浓度的是完全去质子化的草酸根 C2O4^2-。

method.method_draft: Use the graph to estimate the first equivalence volume as 10 mL. With 0.10 M NaOH, that implies the initial H2C2O4 amount is 0.10 mol/L × 0.010 L = 0.001 mol. At 20 mL NaOH added, the moles of OH− are 0.10 mol/L × 0.020 L = 0.002 mol, exactly two equivalents per mole of H2C2O4. Therefore the acid has been fully neutralized to oxalate, so the species in greatest concentration is C2O4^2−.
